title: In April 2020, a barrel of oil briefly cost less than nothing
body: On 20 April 2020, the May futures contract for West Texas Intermediate crude closed at **−$37.63 a barrel**: sellers were paying buyers to take the oil. COVID-19 lockdowns had crushed demand, storage was a problem, and the contract expired the next day, when anyone still holding it would have to take delivery at Cushing, Oklahoma, the settlement point for WTI. Traders with no tanks sold at any price, and so few buyers were left that the exchange’s trade-at-settlement mechanism shut down for the first time ever. The June contract closed the same day at a positive $20.43, so the negative price was about timing and storage, not oil being worthless.

slides.question: On 20 April 2020, where did the May contract for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude close, in dollars a barrel?
slides.explanation: It closed at −$37.63: sellers were paying buyers to take the oil off their hands, because the contract expired the next day with delivery at Cushing. The June contract closed at $20.43.

slides.label: closing price of the May 2020 WTI contract on 20 April 2020
slides.text: The June contract closed at +$20.43 the same day.

slides.heading: Why it went negative
items: The May contract expired the next day, with physical delivery at Cushing
Traders with no tanks sold at any price

slides.heading: What is Cushing?
slides.text: Cushing, Oklahoma, a town of under 8,000 people, is the delivery point for WTI futures and so the price settlement point for the contract on the New York Mercantile Exchange, a role it has held for over three decades.

slides.question: Why did the June contract stay positive on the same day?
options: It was a month from delivery
slides.explanation: The May contract expired the next day and forced delivery at Cushing, while June left a month for storage and demand to change, so it closed at $20.43.

slides.heading: Fact or myth?

items.text: Sellers paid buyers to take the May contract
The June contract also closed below zero
Storage was hard to find as lockdowns cut demand

slides.explanation: It was about timing and storage: holders of the expiring May contract faced delivery at Cushing the next day, while June closed at $20.43.
